entities.name: PMID:23032485
observations: Rat study of graded global cerebral ischemia induced by unilateral carotid occlusion, bilateral carotid occlusion, and more severe occlusion combinations during forepaw stimulation.

Functional metabolic response remained tightly coupled to somatosensory evoked potentials, but flow responses were more strongly attenuated than electrical responses as ischemia became severe, indicating activation-flow uncoupling.

entities.name: PMID:15893740
observations: Rat compression-ischemia study combined cortical compression with ipsilateral common carotid occlusion and measured laser-Doppler flow and evoked potentials during forepaw stimulation.
A visible activation-flow response persisted across 0–90% cortical flow reduction, but its amplitude began declining with mild ischemia and progressively decreased as flow reduction increased.

entities.name: Activation-flow uncoupling
observations: During graded ischemia in rats, forepaw-evoked cerebral blood-flow responses are attenuated more than somatosensory electrical responses.
